label: thm.intro_srw
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.intro_srw}
Fix integers $n, m \ge 2$ and a real $a\ge 1$.
Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(n, a, m)>0$ such that the following holds.

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$,
and $U$ a finite symmetric set in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ of cardinality $m$.

If the group $\<U\>$ generated by $U$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent, then
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(n, a, m)L(U).
\]
head: environment

label: cor.intro_dichotomy
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.intro_dichotomy}
Fix integers $n, m \ge 2$ and a real $a\ge 1$.
Then, there exists a constant $c(n, a, m)>0$ such that the following holds.


Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$, and $U$ a finite symmetric set in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ of cardinality $m$.

If $\<U\>$ is discrete, then 
either $\ell(\mu_U)=0$ or $\ell(\mu_U) \ge c(n, a, m)$.

label: thm.intro_Hn
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.intro_Hn}
Fix an integer $n \ge 2$ and a real $a\ge 1$.
Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group, and 
$\nu$ an admissible probability measure on $\Gamma$ with a finite first moment. 
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite symmetric generating set of $\Gamma$ with $1 \in \Sigma$.

Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(n, a, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)>0$ such that the following holds.

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$. 
For every faithful, isometric action $\rho:\Gamma \to \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ such that $\rho(\Gamma)$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent,
we have
\[
\ell(\nu, \rho)\ge \kappa(n, a, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)L(\rho(\Sigma)).
\]

label: thm.intro_meta
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.intro_meta}
Fix $\delta, {\mathcal D} \ge 0$, integers $N, q\ge 1$, and $\theta_0\in (0, 1]$.
There exists a constant $\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)>0$ such that the following holds.


Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space.
Let $U$ be a finite symmetric set in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ with $1 \in U$ such that
$L(U^N) \ge K_0 \delta+1$.
Assume that the action of $\<U\>$  on $X$ is non-elementary and ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical.

Let $\mu$ be a countably supported  probability measure on $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ with a finite first moment 
satisfying $\min_{u\in U}\mu^{\ast q}(u)\ge \theta_0$.

Then, we have
\[
\ell(\mu)\ge \kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0) L(U).
\]
Here $K_0$ is an absolute constant, and $\mu^{\ast q}$ is the $q$-fold convolution of $\mu$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Fix  $\delta \ge 0$ and positive integers $m_0$ and $m$.
There exists a constant $\kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)>0$ such that the 
following holds. 

Let $G$ be a hyperbolic group, and $U_0$ a finite symmetric generating
set of $G$ of cardinality $m_0$ such that ${\rm Cay}(G,U_0)$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic.

For every finite symmetric set $U$ in $G$ of cardinality $m$ such that $\<U\>$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$,  we have
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m) L(U).
\]

label: thm.intro_mcg
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.intro_mcg}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least two, and let $m$ be a positive integer. 
We consider the action of the mapping class group ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ on the curve graph $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$.
Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(\mathcal S,m)>0$
such that the following holds:

Let $U$ be a finite symmetric set in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ of cardinality $m$ such that $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element 
and is not virtually cyclic.  
Then, for the uniform distribution $\mu_U$ on $U$, we have
$$\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(\mathcal S,m) L(U).$$
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least two, and 
let $m$ be a positive integer. 
Then, there exists a constant $c(\mathcal S, m)>0$ such that the following holds:

For every finite symmetric set $U$ in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ of cardinality $m$, 
we have
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
$\ell(\mu_U) \ge c(\mathcal S, m)$, if
$\<U\>$ contains at least one pseudo-Anosov element, and $\< U\>$ is not virtually cyclic.


\item
Otherwise, $\ell(\mu_U)=0$.
\end{enumerate}

label: lemma.chain
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.chain}
Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic space.
Let $C, R>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item\label{lemma.chain1}
For all $w, x, y, z \in X$,
if $(w, y)_x\le C$, $(x, z)_y\le C+\delta$, 
and
\[
d(x, y)\ge 2C+2\delta+R,
\]
then 
$(w, z)_x\le C+\delta$.
\item\label{lemma.chain2}
For every $(C, D)$-chain $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with $D \ge 2C+2\delta +R$,
we have
\[
d(x_0, x_n) \ge \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(d(x_i, x_{i+1})-2(C+\delta))\ge R n.
\]
\item\label{lemma.chain3}
For every $(C, D)$-chain $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with $D \ge 2C+4\delta+R$,
we have
$(x_0, x_n)_{x_i} \le C+2\delta$
for all $i=0, \dots, n$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The parts \eqref{lemma.chain1}, \eqref{lemma.chain2}, and \eqref{lemma.chain3} are Lemmas 3.5, 3.7, and 3.8 in \cite{G}, respectively, when $R=1$.
The case when $R>0$ is reduced to the case when $R=1$ by considering the  space $(X, (1/R)d)$, which is $(\delta/R)$-hyperbolic.
\qed

label: lemma.quasiaxis
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.quasiaxis}
For a hyperbolic isometry $g$ of $X$,
there exists a path (continuous map) $\alpha: {\mathbb R} \to X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $g(\alpha)=\alpha$ and there exists  $T>0$ such that $g(\alpha(t))=\alpha(t+T)$ for every $t \in {\mathbb R}$.
\item Let $t_1, t_2 \in {\mathbb R}$ with $t_1<t_2$.
Then every geodesic between $\alpha(t_1)$ and $\alpha(t_2)$ and the path $\alpha|_{[t_1, t_2]}:[t_1, t_2]\to X$ of $\alpha$ are in the $\Delta$-neighborhoods of each other,
where $\Delta=1672\delta$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, $\alpha$ can be parametrized by arc length such that $T>0$.

label: lemma.tr
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.tr}
Let $g$ be a hyperbolic isometry on a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic metric space with a $\Delta$-quasi-axis ${\rm Ax}(g)$.
Then for every integer $n>0$ and every point $x \in {\rm Ax}(g)$,
we have
\[
d(x, g^n x)-8\delta-2\Delta \le n{\rm tr}(g).
\]

label: lemma.rectangle
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.rectangle}
Let $\alpha$ be a $\Delta$-quasi-axis in $X$.
For all $x, y \in X$, let $x', y'$ be points in $\alpha$ such that
\[
d(x, x')= d(x, \alpha) \quad \text{and} \quad d(y, y')= d(y, \alpha).
\]
If $d(x', y')> 10\delta+2\Delta$,
then
\[
d(x, x')+d(x', y')+d(y', y)\le d(x, y)+18\delta+4\Delta.
\]
head: environment

label: lemma.tripod
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.tripod}
Let $x, y, z$ in $X$.
For all $y' \in [x, y]$ and all $z'\in [x, z]$ such that $d(x, y')=d(x, z')\le (y,z)_x$,
we have $d(y', z')\le 4\delta$.
head: environment
name: The tripod lemma

title: Proof
body_md:
See \cite[21.- Proposition, Chapitre 2]{GH}.
\qed
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we have $(x, y')_{x'} \le 4 \delta+\Delta$.
Indeed, otherwise, by Lemma \ref{lemma.tripod}, we have $z_1 \in [x, x']$ with $d(z_1, x')>4\delta+\Delta$,
and $z_2\in [x', y']$ with $d(z_1, z_2)\le 4\delta$.
Since $\alpha$ is a $\Delta$-quasi-axis, $d(z_2, \alpha)\le \Delta$.
Concatenating $[x, z_1]$, $[z_1, z_2]$, and a geodesic from $z_2$ to $\alpha$ yields a strictly shorter path than $[x, x']$, which is impossible.

Similarly, $(x', y)_{y'} \le 4\delta+\Delta$.
If $d(x', y')> 10 \delta+2\Delta$,
then $(x, y)_{y'}\le 5\delta+\Delta$ by Lemma \ref{lemma.chain} (i). 
By definition of the Gromov product,
we obtain
\begin{align*}
d(x, x')+d(x', y')+d(y', y)
                                       
\le d(x, y)+18\delta+4\Delta.
\end{align*}
This concludes the proof.
\qed

label: thm.bochi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.bochi}
There is an absolute constant $K>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $X$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space and $U \subset \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ a finite 
set. 
Then, we have
\[
L(U) - K\delta \le \lambda_2(U).
\]
head: environment

label: lemma.independent.2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.independent.2}

Let $X$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space. 
Let $U \subset \operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ be a finite set 
with 
\[
L(U) \ge K_0\delta+1.
\]
Then there exists a hyperbolic isometry $g \in U^2$ such that 
\[
{\rm tr}(g) \ge L(U)+4000\delta+1.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm.bochi}, we have $L(U) - K\delta \le \lambda_2(U)$, namely,
there is an element $g \in  U^2$ such that 
$L(U) - K\delta \le {\rm tr}(g)/2$.
(Consider $g^2$ if necessary for $g\in U$.)

Since $L(U)\ge (2K+4000) \delta+1$, 
this element  $g \in U^2$ satisfies 
\[
{\rm tr}(g) \ge 2L(U)-2K\delta \ge L(U)+4000\delta+1.
\]
Since ${\rm tr}(g)>0$, the element $g$ is a hyperbolic isometry on $X$. 
\qed

label: lemma.CAT0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.CAT0}
If $X$ is a ${\rm CAT}(0)$ metric space and $U$ a finite set of isometries, 
then for every $m\in {\mathbb N}_0$, we have
\[
L(U^m)\ge \frac{\sqrt{m}}{2}L(U).
\]
head: environment

label: lemma.independent
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.independent}
Fix $n\in {\mathbb N}$ and $a \in [1, +\infty)$.
Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$.
Let $\delta$ be the hyperbolicity constant of $\Bbb H^2$, so that $X$ 
is $\delta$-hyperbolic. 

Then, there exists a constant $N=N(n, a)$ such that the following holds:
For every finite set $U$ in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ with $1 \in U$ such that $\<U\>$ is discrete and 
non-virtually-nilpotent, 
we have
\[
L(U^N) \ge K_0 \delta+1.
\]
Here $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Lemma \ref{lemma.independent.2}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let ${\varepsilon}(n, a)$ denote the Margulis constant of $X$.
The Margulis lemma states that if $\<U\>$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent,
then $L(U)\ge {\varepsilon}(n, a)$, see \cite[Section 8.3]{BGS}.
By Lemma \ref{lemma.CAT0},
we have
\[
L(U^m)\ge \frac{\sqrt{m}}{2}L(U) \ge \frac{\sqrt{m}}{2}{\varepsilon}(n, a),
\]
for every $m \in {\mathbb N}_0$.

Letting 
\[
N:=\left\lceil\left(\frac{2K_0\delta+2}{{\varepsilon}(n, a)}\right)^2 \right\rceil,
\]
we obtain the claim since $N$ depends only on $n$ and $a$.
Here, we denote by $\lceil r \rceil$ the smallest integer greater than or equal to $r \in \Bbb R$.
\qed

label: def.wa
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def.wa}
An isometric action by a group $G$ on a $\delta$-hyperbolic space $X$ 
 is called {\it weakly acylindrical} if
there exists a constant ${\mathcal D} > 0$ such that for every hyperbolic element $g \in G$, 
and every $h \not \in E(g)$, we have
\[
\operatorname{diam} \left(\pi_{{\rm Ax}(g)}(h{\rm Ax}(g))\right) \le {\mathcal D}\left(1+{\rm tr}(g)\right).
\]
We call it ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical if we want to make the constant ${\mathcal D}$ explicit.
head: environment
name: Weak acylindricity

label: lemma.diam
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.diam}
Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ be $\Delta$-quasi-axes of some hyperbolic isometries in a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic metric space $X$.
For every $R\ge 0$, we have
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\alpha\cap {\mathcal{N}}_{R}(\beta)) \le \operatorname{diam} \pi_\alpha(\beta) +4R.
\]
Conversely, we have
\[
\operatorname{diam} \pi_\alpha(\beta) \le \operatorname{diam}(\alpha\cap {\mathcal{N}}_{20\delta+2\Delta}(\beta))+10\delta+2\Delta.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the first inequality.
We assume that $\alpha\cap {\mathcal{N}}_{R}(\beta)\neq \emptyset$ since otherwise the inequality holds.
For every $x \in \alpha \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{R}(\beta)$, 
let $y \in \beta$ with $d(x, y) \le R$.
Since $d(y, \pi_\alpha(y)) \le R$,
we have $x \in {\mathcal{N}}_{2R}(\pi_\alpha(\beta))$.
Hence
\[
\alpha \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{R}(\beta) \subset {\mathcal{N}}_{2R}(\pi_\alpha(\beta)),
\]
implying the first inequality.


We show the second inequality.
Let $a_1, a_2\in \alpha$. 
Further, let $b_1, b_2\in \beta$ be points such that $a_i \in \pi_{\alpha}(b_i)$, $i=1, 2$.
We consider a geodesic rectangle on $a_1, a_2, b_2, b_1$.

Suppose $d(a_1, a_2)>10\delta+2\Delta$.
As in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma.rectangle}, we have
\[
(b_1, a_2)_{a_1} \le 4\delta+\Delta \quad \text{and} \quad (b_1, b_2)_{a_2} \le 5\delta+\Delta.
\]
Thus,
by definition of the Gromov product, we obtain
\[
(a_1, b_1)_{a_2}=d(a_1, a_2)-(b_1, a_2)_{a_1} \ge d(a_1, a_2)-4\delta-\Delta>5\delta+\Delta\ge (b_1, b_2)_{a_2}.
\]
Consider geodesic triangles on $a_1, a_2, b_1$, and on $b_1, a_2, b_2$.
By using the tripod lemma (Lemma \ref{lemma.tripod}), 
we have
\[
d(a_1, \beta) \le 12 \delta+2\Delta \quad \text{and} \quad d(a_2, \beta)\le 9\delta+2\Delta.
\]
Thus, $a_1, a_2 \in \alpha \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{12\delta+2\Delta}(\beta)$.
Therefore, if $\operatorname{diam} \pi_\alpha(\beta)>10\delta+2\Delta$,
then
$\operatorname{diam} \pi_\alpha(\beta) \le \operatorname{diam} (\alpha \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{20\delta+2\Delta}(\beta))$.
The desired second inequality follows by
combining the case when $\operatorname{diam} \pi_\alpha(\beta)\le 10\delta+2\Delta$,
completing the proof.
\qed

label: prop.overlap
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.overlap}
There exists a constant $Z>0$ that depends only on $n$ and $a$ with
the following property. 
Let $G < \operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ be a discrete group on $X$, 
and $g\in G$ hyperbolic.   
For every $h\in G$ such that $ h \not\in E(g)$, 
we have
\[
\operatorname{diam} \left({\rm Ax}(g) \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{50\delta}(h{\rm Ax}(g))\right) \le (n+2) {\rm tr}(g) + Z.
\]
head: environment

label: cor.Hn
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.Hn}
Let $n \in {\mathbb N}$ and $a \in [1, +\infty)$.
Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold $X$ with sectional curvature $K_X\in [-a^2, -1]$.
Let $G <\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ be a discrete subgroup. 

Then there exists a constant ${\mathcal D}={\mathcal D}(n, a)$ such that the action of $G$ on $X$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical.
head: environment
name: Weak-acylindricity

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta$ be a hyperbolicity constant of $\mathbb H^2$.
Then $X$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic.
As we said, since the axis of a hyperbolic isometry of $X$ is
a geodesic, we may take $\Delta=0$ in Lemma \ref{lemma.diam}.

Let $g\in G$ be hyperbolic and $h\in G\setminus E(g)$.
By Lemma \ref{lemma.diam} and Proposition \ref{prop.overlap}, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{diam}\pi_{{\rm Ax}(g)}
  (h{\rm Ax}(g))
&\le
\operatorname{diam} \left(
  {\rm Ax}(g) \cap
  {\mathcal{N}}_{20\delta}(h{\rm Ax}(g)) \right)
  +10\delta\\
&\le (n+2) {\rm tr}(g)+Z+10\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Setting
$
\mathcal D=\max\{n+2,Z+10\delta\},
$
we obtain the claim. Note that $\mathcal D$ depends
only on $n$ and $a$.
\qed

label: lemma.nonelem
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemmas \ref{lemma.independent} and \ref{lemma.independent.2}, $\<U\>$ contains a hyperbolic element $g$. Let $E(g)$ be the elementary closure in $\<U\>$. 
Then, $E(g)$ is virtually cyclic since it preserves $\operatorname{{\rm Ax}}(g)$
and $E(g)$ is discrete.
It implies that $\< U\> \not\subset E(g)$
since $\<U\>$ is not virtually-nilpotent. 

Let $u \in \<U \> \backslash E(g)$. 
Set $h=ugu^{-1} \in \< U\>$, which is hyperbolic. Then $g$ and $h$ are independent. 
Indeed, otherwise, $g$ and $h$ fix a common point in $\partial X$.
Then, $\operatorname{diam} \pi_{\operatorname{{\rm Ax}}(g)} (u \operatorname{{\rm Ax}}(g))$ is infinite. 
This contradicts Corollary \ref{cor.Hn} since it in particular says that 
$\operatorname{diam} \pi_{\operatorname{{\rm Ax}}(g)} (u \operatorname{{\rm Ax}}(g))$ is finite.
\qed

title: Definition
body_md:
Fix a point $o \in X$.
Let $\eta, C, D \ge 0$. 
A finite set $S$ of isometries of $X$ is $(\eta, C, D)$-{\bf Schottky} at $o$ if the following holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item For all $x, y \in X$, 
we have
$\#\{s \in S \ : \ (sx, y)_o \le C\} \ge (1-\eta)\#S$.
\item For all $x, y \in X$,
we have 
$\#\{s \in S \ : \ (s^{-1}x, y)_o \le C\} \ge (1-\eta)\#S$.
\item 
For all $s\in S$, 
we have $d(o, so) \ge D$.
\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: lemma.free
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.free}
Fix $o \in X$.
Let $C, D > 0$. 
Let $\{u, u'\} \subset \operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$.
Suppose that the following holds:
\[
\max\big\{(so, s'o)_o \ : \ s, s' \in \{u, u^{-1}, u', u'^{-1}\}, s\neq s'\big\} \le C,
\]
and 
\[
\min\big\{d(o, u o), d(o, u' o)\big\}\ge D.
\]
If $D > 2C+2\delta$, then $\{u, u'\}$ freely generates a free subgroup in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let  $w$ and $w'$ be non-empty reduced words on $\{u, u^{-1}, u', u'^{-1}\}$ of length $n$ and $m$, respectively:
\[
w=s_1\cdots s_n \quad \text{and} \quad w'=s'_1\cdots s'_m
\]
with $s_i, s_i'\in \{u, u^{-1}, u', u'^{-1}\}$.
We may assume that $n \le m$.

Let $k$ be the largest $i \le n$ such that $s_j=s_j'$ for all $j \in \{1, \dots, i\}$ if it exists, $k:=0$ if otherwise.
If $w\neq w'$ as words,
then $k<m$,
and the following sequence forms a $(C, D)$-chain:
\[
s_{k+1}\cdots s_n o,
s_{k+1}\cdots s_{n-1} o, \dots, s_{k+1}o, o, s'_{k+1}o, \dots, s'_{k+1}\cdots s'_m o.
\]
Since $k<m$, the sequence consists of at least two points.
If $D > 2C+2\delta$, we have $wo\neq w'o$ by Lemma \ref{lemma.chain} \eqref{lemma.chain2}.
This implies that $w\neq w'$ as isometries.
Therefore, the inclusion $\{u, u'\} \to \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ extends to an injective homomorphism from the free group on $\{u, u'\}$ to $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$, yielding the claim.
\qed
head: manual

label: lemma.criterion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.criterion}
For a finite set $S$ of isometries of $X$ with $S=S^{-1}$,
let
\[
C_0=\max_{s_1\neq s_2, s_1, s_2 \in S}(s_1o, s_2o)_o
\quad
\text{and}
\quad 
D_0=\min_{s \in S}d(o, so).
\]
If $D_0>2C_0+4\delta$,
then
$S$ is $(\eta, C_0+3\delta, D_0)$-Schottky at $o$ with
$\eta=2/\# S$.

label: prop.schottky
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.schottky}
Let $N \in {\mathbb N}$ and $\delta, {\mathcal D} \ge 0$.
Let $X$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space. 
Let $U$ be a finite set of isometries in $X$ with $1 \in U$ and $U=U^{-1}$. 
Let $g$ be a hyperbolic isometry of $X$.
Suppose that the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item\label{assump.h}  $U^N$ contains $g$ such that 
${\rm tr}(g) \ge L(U)+4000\delta+1$.
\item\label{assump.action}
$\<U\>$ does not preserve the set of fixed points of $g$ in $\partial X$.

\item\label{assump.wa} The action of $\langle U\rangle$ on $X$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a positive integer $M=M(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$, a point $o\in X$, and positive constants $C(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$ and $D(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$ such that the following holds:


\begin{itemize}
\item 
We have $D\ge 20C+100\delta+L(U)$ for  
\[
C=C(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1) \quad \text{and} \quad D=D(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1).
\]


\item $U^M$ contains a $(1/100, C, D)$-Schottky set $S$ at $o$. 

\item We have $\# S \ge 200$.
\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: lemma.tube
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.tube}
Under the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop.schottky},
we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq.tube1}
o\in {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(g))\cap {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(h)),
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda=NL(U)+4000\delta+1$. 
Furthermore, for every $m \in {\mathbb Z}$, we have
\[
\max\{(g^m o, h^m o)_o, (g^m o, h^{-m} o)_o\} \le {\mathcal D}({\rm tr}(g)+1)+10\Lambda+100\delta.
\]
head: environment

label: eq.tube2
title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove that $o \in {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(g))$.
Suppose, to the contrary, that $o\notin {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(g))$.
Since $1\in U$, we have $\{g, h\} \subset U^{N+2}$, and thus, by Lemma \ref{lemma.disp} \eqref{item.Un},
\[
L(\{g, h\}) \le L(U^{N+2}) \le (N+2)L(U).
\]
On the one hand, 
by \eqref{eq.basepoint},
\begin{align}\label{eq.tube2}
d(o, g o)	
\le L(\{g, h\})+1
\le (N+2)L(U)+1.
\end{align}
On the other hand,
since $o \notin {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(g))$,
we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq.tube3}
2\Lambda+{\rm tr}(g) \le d(o, g o)+8000\delta.
\end{equation}
To see this, 
choose the points $o, x, g x, g o$ where $x \in {\rm Ax}(g)$ with $d(o, x)= d(o, {\rm Ax}(g))$.
Note that $d(x, g x)\ge {\rm tr}(g) \ge 4000\delta$ by definition of ${\rm tr}(g)$ and the assumption \eqref{assump.h}.
Then, Lemma \ref{lemma.rectangle} shows \eqref{eq.tube3}.

Combining \eqref{eq.tube2} and \eqref{eq.tube3},
we obtain
\[
2\Lambda+{\rm tr}(g) \le (N+2)L(U)+8000\delta+1.
\]
Since ${\rm tr}(g) \ge L(U)+4000\delta+1$ by the assumption \eqref{assump.h},
this implies 
\[
2\Lambda\le (N+1)L(U)+4000\delta.
\]
This is a contradiction since $\Lambda=NL(U)+4000\delta+1$.
Thus, we have shown $o \in {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(g))$.

Similarly, $o \in {\mathcal{N}}_{\Lambda}({\rm Ax}(h))$ since ${\rm tr}(h)={\rm tr}(g)$ and \eqref{eq.basepoint} holds.
Thus, we obtain \eqref{eq.tube1}.



It suffices to prove the second claim for $g^m$ and $h^m$ with $m \ge 0$
since the case for $m <0$ follows by replacing $g$ and $h$ with their inverses. 



We show that
for every $m\ge 0$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq.tube4}
(g^m o, h^m o)_o -2\Lambda -8\delta\le \operatorname{diam} ({\rm Ax}(g)\cap{\mathcal{N}}_{2\Lambda+20\delta}({\rm Ax}(h))).
\end{equation}
We consider a geodesic triangle on $o$, $g^m o$, and $h^m o$.
First, by \eqref{eq.tube1},
we have $x \in {\rm Ax}(g)$ and $y \in {\rm Ax}(h)$ such that $d(o, x) \le \Lambda$ and $d(o, y) \le \Lambda$.
Furthermore, by the property of quasi-axes (Lemma \ref{lemma.quasiaxis} (i)),
we have $g^m x \in {\rm Ax}(g)$ and $h^m y \in {\rm Ax}(h)$.
Next, by the tripod lemma (Lemma \ref{lemma.tripod}),
there exist $p \in [o, g^m o]$ and $q \in [o, h^m o]$ such that
\[
d(o, p)=d(o, q)=(g^m o, h^m o)_o \quad \text{and} \quad d(p, q) \le 4\delta.
\]
Furthermore, since 
$d(g^m o, g^m x) \le \Lambda$ and $d(h^m o, h^m y)\le \Lambda$,
we have
\[
d(p, {\rm Ax}(g)) \le \Lambda+8\delta \quad \text{and} \quad d(q, {\rm Ax}(h)) \le \Lambda+8\delta.
\]
The first inequality follows by considering a geodesic rectangle on $o, x, g^m x, g^m o$ and applying the tripod lemma (Lemma \ref{lemma.tripod}) twice, and the second inequality follows similarly.
Let $p' \in {\rm Ax}(g)$ and $q' \in {\rm Ax}(h)$ with $d(p, p') \le \Lambda+8\delta$ and $d(q, q')\le \Lambda+8\delta$, respectively.
By the triangle inequality, we have
$d(x, y) \le 2\Lambda$ and $d(p', q') \le 2\Lambda+20\delta$.
Thus, we obtain
\[
x, p' \in {\rm Ax}(g) \cap {\mathcal{N}}_{2\Lambda+20\delta}({\rm Ax}(h)).
\]
Since by the triangle inequality $d(o, p) \le d(x, p')+2\Lambda+8\delta$, we have
\[
(g^m o, h^m o)_o-2\Lambda-8\delta \le d(x, p')\le \operatorname{diam}\left({\rm Ax}(g)\cap {\mathcal{N}}_{2\Lambda+20\delta}({\rm Ax}(h))\right).
\]
This shows \eqref{eq.tube4}.


We now use the ${\mathcal D}$-weak acylindricity of the isometric action of $\langle U\rangle$ on $X$ in the assumption \eqref{assump.wa}.
By Definition \ref{def.wa} and Lemma \ref{lemma.diam},
we have:
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{diam}({\rm Ax}(g)\cap{\mathcal{N}}_{2\Lambda+20\delta}({\rm Ax}(h)))
&\le \operatorname{diam} (\pi_{{\rm Ax}(g)}{{\rm Ax}(h)})+4(2\Lambda+20\delta)\\
&\le {\mathcal D}({\rm tr}(g)+1)+8\Lambda+80\delta.
\end{align*}
Rearranging the terms, we obtain the claim.
\qed
head: manual

label: lemma.separation
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we show \eqref{eq.qa}.
Let us show the required bound on $(g^m o, g^{-m}o)_o$ for every integer $m \ge 1$, 
as the Gromov product equals $0$ when $m=0$.
The bound on $(h^m o, h^{-m}o)_o$ follows analogously.

By Lemma \ref{lemma.tube}, there exists $x \in {\rm Ax}(g)$ such that $d(o, x)\le \Lambda$.
For every $m\ge 1$, 
since ${\rm tr}(g) > 4000\delta$ by the assumption \eqref{assump.h},
we have
\[
d(g^{-m}x, g^m x)=d(x, g^{2m} x) \ge {\rm tr}(g^{2m})=2m{\rm tr}(g) > 8000m\delta.
\]
Applying Lemma \ref{lemma.rectangle} to $g^{-m}o$, $g^{-m}x$, $g^m x$, $g^m o$,
we obtain 
\[
2d(o, x)+d(g^{-m}x, g^m x) \le d(g^{-m}o, g^m o)+8000\delta.
\]
Since $g^{-m}x, x, g^m x$ belong to ${\rm Ax}(g)$, and ${\rm Ax}(g)$ is a $\Delta$-quasi-axis,
the $\Delta$-neighborhood of a geodesic $[g^{-m}x, g^m x]$ contains $x$.
Thus, we have
\[
d(g^{-m}x, x)+d(x, g^m x) \le d(g^{-m}x, g^m x)+2\Delta.
\]
Therefore, we obtain
\[
2d(o, x)+d(g^{-m}x, x)+d(x, g^m x) \le d(g^{-m}o, g^m o)+8000\delta+2\Delta.
\]
By definition of the Gromov product and the triangle inequality,
we obtain:
\begin{align*}
(g^{-m}o, g^m o)_o
&=\frac{1}{2}(d(o, g^{-m}o)+d(o, g^m o)-d(g^{-m}o, g^m o))\\
&\le \frac{1}{2}(4d(o, x)+d(x, g^{-m}x)+d(x, g^m x)-d(g^{-m}o, g^m o))\\
&\le d(o, x)+4000\delta+\Delta\le \Lambda+4000\delta+\Delta.
\end{align*}
Recall that $\Lambda=NL(U)+4000\delta+1$. 
Moreover, $\Delta\le 2000\delta$ by Lemma \ref{lemma.quasiaxis}.
Thus, we have
\[
\Lambda+\Delta+4000\delta \le NL(U)+10^4\delta+1\le C_0(\delta, N)(L(U)+1).
\]
This implies \eqref{eq.qa}.

Next, we show \eqref{eq.wa}.
Since $g \in U^N$,
by Lemma \ref{lemma.disp}, we have ${\rm tr}(g) \le N L(U)$.
By Lemma \ref{lemma.tube}, 
for every $m \ge 0$,
we have
\begin{align*}
(g^m o, h^m o)_o 
&\le {\mathcal D}({\rm tr}(g)+1)+10\Lambda+100\delta\\
&\le {\mathcal D}(N L(U)+1)+10(NL(U)+4000\delta+1)+100\delta\\
&\le ({\mathcal D} N+10N+10^5\delta+10)(L(U)+1).
\end{align*}
For every $m \ge 0$, we have
\[
(g^m o, h^m o)_o \le C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1),
\]
where $C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)={\mathcal D} N+10N+10^5\delta+10$.
The same inequality holds for $(g^m o, h^{-m}o)_o$.
Thus, we have \eqref{eq.wa}.

Finally, we show \eqref{eq.D} and \eqref{eq.Dup}.
Since ${\rm tr}(g)={\rm tr}(g^{-1})$,
by the assumption \eqref{assump.h}, for every $m \in {\mathbb Z}$, we have
\[
d(o, g^m o) \ge {\rm tr}(g^m)=|m|{\rm tr}(g) \ge |m|(L(U)+1).
\]
The analogous inequality holds for $d(o, h^m o)$ since ${\rm tr}(g)={\rm tr}(h)$.
Hence we obtain \eqref{eq.D}.
Furthermore, 
we have
\[
d(o, g^m o) \le |m|((N+2)L(U)+1),
\]
by the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq.basepoint}, and Lemma \ref{lemma.disp} \eqref{item.Un} since $\{g, h\}\subset U^{N+2}$.
The analogous inequality holds for $d(o, h^m o)$.
Thus, we obtain \eqref{eq.Dup}.
\qed
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $n, m, r \in {\mathbb N}$,
let
\[
S_{n, m, r}:=\Big\{ (u_1\cdots u_n)^r, (u_1\cdots u_n)^{-r} \ : \ u_i \in \{g^m, h^m\}, i=1, \dots, n\Big\}.
\]
Note that $S_{n, m, r} \subset U^{(N+2)nmr}$ since $U=U^{-1}$.
We will show that $S_{n, m, r}$ is a required Schottky set at $o$ for appropriately chosen $n$, $m$, and $r$.
As we will see, these integers depend only on ${\mathcal D}$, $N$, and $\delta$,
and we will define 
$M=(N+2)nmr$.


By Lemma \ref{lemma.separation} \eqref{eq.qa} and \eqref{eq.wa},
we have a constant $C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)>0$ such that
for every $m \in {\mathbb N}$ and for all $s, s' \in \{g^m, g^{-m}, h^m, h^{-m}\}$ with $s\neq s'$,
\[
(s o, s' o)_o \le C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1).
\]
Furthermore, by \eqref{eq.D}, we have
\[
\min\left\{d(o, g^{m} o), d(o, h^{m}o)\right\} \ge m(L(U)+1).
\]
Set
\[
m:=\lceil 2C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)+4\delta+1 \rceil.
\]
For
$C_1:=C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1)$ and $D_1:=m(L(U)+1)$,
we have
\begin{align*}
D_1=m(L(U)+1)
&\ge 2C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1)+4\delta+L(U)+1\\
&=2C_1+4\delta+L(U)+1.
\end{align*}
In particular, we have $D_1>2C_1+2\delta$, hence,
by Lemma \ref{lemma.free}, $\{g^m, h^m\}$ freely generates a free subgroup in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$.
Thus, we have
$\# S_{n, m, r}=2^{n+1}$.
Set
\[
n:=\lceil \log_2 100 \rceil,
\]
so that $\# S_{n, m, r}\ge 200$.




We consider each $w \in S_{n, m, r}$ as a reduced word on $\{g^m, g^{-m}, h^m, h^{-m}\}$ of length $nr$.
For every pair of such reduced words
\[
w=s_1\cdots s_{nr} \quad \text{and} \quad w'=s_1'\cdots s_{nr}',  \quad \text{where $s_i, s_i'\in \{g^m, g^{-m}, h^m, h^{-m}\}$},
\]
let $k$ be the largest $i \le n$ such that $s_j=s_j'$ for all $j \in \{1, \dots, i\}$.
We note that each element in $S_{n, m, r}$ is the $r$-th power of a word of length $n$.
Hence, if $w\neq w'$ as words,
then $k<n$.
By definition of the Gromov product, 
we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq.gp_o}
(wo, w'o)_o \le d(o, s_1\cdots s_k o)+(wo, w'o)_{s_1\cdots s_k o}.
\end{equation}
Note that $d(o, s_1\cdots s_k o)\le (n-1)m((N+2)L(U)+1)$ by \eqref{eq.Dup} since $k< n$.
Moreover, since $D_1>2C_1+4\delta$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq.gp_k}
(wo, w'o)_{s_1\cdots s_k o} \le C_1+2\delta=C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1)+2\delta,
\end{equation}
for a $(C_1, D_1)$-chain by Lemma \ref{lemma.chain} \eqref{lemma.chain3}.
Combining \eqref{eq.gp_o} with \eqref{eq.gp_k},
we obtain the following:
for all $w, w' \in S_{n, m, r}$ with $w\neq w'$,
\begin{align*}
(wo, w'o)_o 
\le C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N) (L(U)+1),
\end{align*}
where $C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N):=(n-1)m(N+2)+C_1(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)+2\delta$.
Note that $C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$ is a constant depending only on $\delta$, ${\mathcal D}$, and $N$.
Furthermore, $C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)>  3\delta$ since $m > 3\delta$.



For each $w \in S_{n, m, r}$, 
by Lemma \ref{lemma.chain} \eqref{lemma.chain2} applied to a $(C_1, D_1)$-chain of length $nr$,
we have
$d(o, wo) \ge nr(L(U)+1)$.
Set
\[
r:=\lceil 40C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)+100\delta+1 \rceil.
\]
Then, since $n\ge 1$, we have
\[
nr (L(U)+1) \ge 40C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N) (L(U)+1)+100\delta+L(U).
\]

Summarizing the above discussion, we obtain the following:
Let
\[
C_0:=C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N) (L(U)+1) \quad \text{and} \quad D_0:=nr (L(U)+1).
\]
Then, we have
\[
\max_{w_1\neq w_2, w_1, w_2 \in S_{n, m, r}}(w_1 o, w_2 o)_o \le C_0 \quad \text{and} \quad \min_{w\in S_{n, m, r}}d(o, w o) \ge D_0,
\]
satisfying $D_0>2C_0+4\delta$.
Since $S_{n,m,r}$ is a finite symmetric set with $\# S_{n, m, r}\ge 200$,
Lemma \ref{lemma.criterion} implies that $S_{n, m, r}$ is a $(1/100, C_0+3\delta, D_0)$-Schottky set at o.
Furthermore, by construction, we have
\[
D_0\ge 40 C_0 +100\delta+L(U). 
\]
Letting
$C(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N):=2C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$ and $D(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N):=nr$,
we define
\[
C:=C(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1) \quad \text{and} \quad D:=D(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)(L(U)+1).
\]
Then, since $C=2C_0$ and $C_2(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)\ge 3\delta$, we have $C_0+3\delta\le C$, and $D=D_0$.
Thus, $S_{n, m, r}$ is a $(1/100, C, D)$-Schottky set at $o$ satisfying that
\[
D \ge 20 C+100\delta+L(U).
\]

Finally, setting $M=M(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N):=(N+2)nmr$,
we have $S_{n, m, r}\subset U^M$.
As we have shown above, $\# S_{n, m, r}\ge 200$.
Therefore, the set $S:=S_{n, m, r}$ is a required Schottky set at $o$.
This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop.schottky}.
\qed

label: eq:ldp
title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Lemma 4.9]{G}, for all $i \in {\mathbb Z}$,
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(\#P_{n+1}\ge i)\ge \operatorname{{\bf P}}(\#P_n+U \ge i),
\]
where $U$ is a random variable independent from $\#P_n$ distributed as
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(U=-j)=9\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{j+1} \ \text{for $j>0$}, \
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(U=0)=0 \ \text{and} \
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(U=1)=\frac{9}{10}. 
\]
Thus, letting $U_i$, $i\in {\mathbb N}$, be independent copies of $U$, independently from the sequence $\# P_n$, $n\in {\mathbb N}_0$, for each $i\in {\mathbb Z}$ and each $n \in {\mathbb N}$, we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(\# P_n\ge i)\ge \operatorname{{\bf P}}(U_1+\cdots+U_n \ge i).
\]
Therefore, for every $r>0$ and every $n \in {\mathbb N}_0$, we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(\# P_n \le r n) \le \operatorname{{\bf P}}(U_1+\cdots+U_n \le r n).
\]
We show that for every $r\in (0, \operatorname{{\bf E}} U)$, there exists $c_r>0$ such that
for all $n \in {\mathbb N}_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ldp}
\operatorname{{\bf P}}(U_1+\cdots+U_n \le r n) \le e^{-c_r n}.
\end{equation}
This implies the claim by taking $r=1/2<\operatorname{{\bf E}} U=71/90$.

Let us show \eqref{eq:ldp}.
For every $r \in (0, \operatorname{{\bf E}} U)$, define ${\varepsilon}:=\operatorname{{\bf E}} U-r>0$.
For every $t>0$, by the Markov inequality and the independence of $U_i$, $i\in {\mathbb N}$, we have the following:
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{{\bf P}}\Big(U_1+\cdots+U_n \le rn\Big) 
&=\operatorname{{\bf P}}\Big(-\sum_{i=1}^n (U_i-\operatorname{{\bf E}} U) \ge {\varepsilon} n\Big)\\
&\le e^{-t {\varepsilon} n}\Big(\operatorname{{\bf E}} e^{-t(U-\operatorname{{\bf E}} U)}\Big)^n.
\end{align*}
                                            
Since $\operatorname{{\bf E}} e^{-t (U-\operatorname{{\bf E}} U)}=e^{o(t)}$,
for a small enough $t>0$ with ${\varepsilon}_t:={\varepsilon} -o(t)/t>0$,
the last term in the above displayed inequality is at most $\exp(-t{\varepsilon}_t n)$ for all $n \in {\mathbb N}_0$.
Setting $c_r:=t {\varepsilon}_t>0$ yields \eqref{eq:ldp}.
This completes the proof.

label: prop.drift
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.drift}
Let $\delta, C_0, D\ge 0$, $Q\in {\mathbb N}$, and $\theta \in (0, 1]$.
Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic space.
Fix an arbitrary $o \in X$.
Let $S \subset \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ be a $(1/100, C_0, D)$-Schottky set at $o \in X$ such that
$D \ge 20 C_0+100\delta+1$,
and $\mu$ be a countably supported probability measure  on $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ with $\mu^{\ast Q} \ge \theta \mu_S^{\ast 2}$.


Then there exists a constant $c_\theta>0$ such that for all $n \ge 4Q/\theta$,
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(\frac{1}{n}d(o, w_n o) \le \frac{\kappa\theta}{4Q} \right)\le 2 \exp\left(-\frac{c_\theta}{4Q} n\right).
\]
In particular,
for $\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu$-almost every $(w_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0} \in G^{{\mathbb N}_0}$,
we have
\[
\liminf_{n \to +\infty}\frac{1}{n}d(o, w_n o) \ge \frac{\kappa\theta}{4Q},
\]
where $\kappa$ is the universal constant in Proposition \ref{prop.pivot}.

label: lemma.lazy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.lazy}
Let $\mu$ be a countably supported probability measure of finite first moment on $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$. Set
$\widetilde \mu:=(\mu+\delta_1)/2$.
Then,
we have
$\ell(\widetilde \mu)=\ell(\mu)/2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(\chi_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$ be an i.i.d.\ $(\{0, 1\}, 1/2)$-Bernoulli random variables,
and $t_n:=\chi_1+\cdots+\chi_n$.
Then, a $\widetilde \mu$-random walk $(\widetilde w_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$ has the same distribution as that of $(w_{t_n})_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$ where $(w_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$ is a $\mu$-random walk.
Since $t_n/n \to 1/2$, as $n \to \infty$, almost surely by the strong law of large numbers,
we have $\ell(\widetilde \mu)=\ell(\mu)/2$ by definition of the drift.
\qed

label: thm.meta
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.meta}
Let $\delta, {\mathcal D} \ge 0$, $N, q \in {\mathbb N}$, and $\theta_0\in (0, 1]$.
Then there exist constants $\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)>0$ and $c_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)>0$ such that the following holds. 



Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space.
Let $U$ be a finite symmetric set in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ with $1 \in U$. 
Assume 
$L(U^N) \ge K_0 \delta+1$. Assume that the action of $\<U\>$  on $X$
is  non-elementary and ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical.

Let $\mu$ be a countably supported probability measure on $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$
with 
$$\min_{u\in U}\mu^{\ast q}(u)\ge \theta_0.$$





Then, for all large enough $n$,
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\Bigg(\frac{1}{n L(U)}d(o, w_n o) \le \kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0) \Bigg)\le  \exp\Bigg(-c_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0) n\Bigg).
\]
Consequently, if $\mu$ has a finite first moment, then
\[
\ell(\mu)\ge \kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0) L(U).
\]
Moreover, there exists $M\in {\mathbb N}$ depending only on $\delta$, ${\mathcal D}$, and $N$, such that
\[
\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)=\frac{\theta_0^{2M}}{16qM}.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
To apply Proposition \ref{prop.schottky}, we first check its assumptions. 
First, since $L(U^N) \ge K_0\delta+1$, Lemma \ref{lemma.independent.2} implies that
there exists a hyperbolic element $g \in U^{2N}$ such that
\[
{\rm tr}(g)\ge L(U)+4000\delta+1.
\]
Second, since the action of $\<U\>$ on $X$ is non-elementary,  $\<U\>$ does not preserve the set of fixed points of $g$ in $\partial X$.
Lastly, since the action of $\<U\>$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical, 
we apply Proposition \ref{prop.schottky} and  obtain the following: 

There exists an integer $M=M(\delta, {\mathcal D}, 2N)$ and a point $o\in X$ such that $U^M$ contains a $(1/100, C, D)$-Schottky set $S$ at $o$
with
$D\ge 20C+100\delta+L(U)$, where
$C=C(\delta, {\mathcal D}, 2N)(L(U)+1)$ and $D=D(\delta, {\mathcal D}, 2N)(L(U)+1)$.

We will apply Proposition \ref{prop.drift}.
Since $U^{2M} \supset S^2$, and by assumption  $\min_{u \in U}\mu^{\ast q}(u) \ge \theta_0$,
we have
\[
\mu^{\ast (2Mq)} \ge \theta_0^{2M}\boldsymbol{1}_{S^2} \ge \theta_0^{2M}\mu_S^{\ast 2}.
\]
Here $\boldsymbol{1}_E$ denotes the indicator function on a set $E$ and $\mu_S$ denotes the uniform distribution on $S$.

Let $Q:=2Mq$ and $\theta:=\theta_0^{2M}$, so that $\mu^{\ast Q} \ge \theta \mu_S^{\ast 2}$.
Let $R:=L(U)>0$.
After rescaling the metric by $R^{-1}$,  the metric space $(X, R^{-1}d)$ is $(\delta/R)$-hyperbolic.
With respect to the rescaled metric, the set $S$   is 
a $(1/100, C/R, D/R)$-Schottky set  at $o$ on $(X, R^{-1}d)$, where 
\[
D/R\ge 20 (C/R)+100(\delta/R)+1.
\]
Applying Proposition \ref{prop.drift} to this setting, 
there exists a constant $c_\theta>0$ such that for all $n \ge 4Q/\theta$,
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(\frac{1}{nL(U)}d(o, w_n o) \le \frac{\kappa\theta}{4Q} \right)\le 2 \exp\left(-\frac{c_\theta}{4Q} n\right),
\]
where $\kappa$ is the universal constant in Proposition \ref{prop.pivot}.
Letting 
\[
\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0):=\frac{\kappa\theta}{4Q}=\frac{\kappa \theta_0^{2M}}{8Mq}
\quad \text{and} \quad
c_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0):=\frac{c_\theta}{8Q}=\frac{c_\theta}{16Mq}
\]
we obtain the first claim.

Furthermore, 
for $\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu$-almost every $(w_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$,
\[
\liminf_{n\to +\infty}\frac{1}{Rn}d(o, w_n o) \ge \kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0).
\]

If $\mu$ has a finite first moment, the Kingman subadditive ergodic theorem 
implies that the above liminf is in fact a limit, and is equal to $\ell(\mu)/R$ for $\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu$-almost every $(w_n)_{n \in {\mathbb N}_0}$.

Finally, we obtain the explicit value of the constant $\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)$ by  taking $\kappa=1/2$ as allowed by Proposition \ref{prop.kappa}.
\qed

we assume that $\mu$ is bounded.
Then, 
for sufficiently large  $n$, 
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(\frac{1}{nL(U)}{\rm tr}(w_n) \le \frac{1}{2}\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)\right) \le  \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}c_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)n\right).

label: lemma.BMSS
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.BMSS}
For any $\zeta>0$ and any ${\varepsilon}>0$,
there is an integer $N \in {\mathbb N}_0$ such that for any $n \ge N$, 
we have
\[
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left({\rm tr}(w_n) \le \zeta n\right) \le (n+1)\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(d(o, w_n o)\le (\zeta+{\varepsilon})n\right).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Letting $\zeta={\varepsilon}=(1/2)\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)$,
we apply Lemma \ref{lemma.BMSS} to the present setting where the metric is rescaled by $1/L(U)$:
there exists an integer $N$ such that for all $n \ge N$, 
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(\frac{1}{nL(U)}{\rm tr}(w_n) \le \zeta\right)
\le (n+1)\operatorname{{\bf P}}_\mu\left(\frac{1}{nL(U)}d(o, w_n o)\le 2 \zeta\right).
\end{align*}
Furthermore, by Theorem \ref{thm.meta}, the right hand side is bounded from above by
\[
(n+1) \exp\left(-c n\right)=\exp\left(-cn+\log(n+1)\right)
\le 
\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}c n\right)
\]
for sufficiently large $n$, where $c=c_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)>0$.
\qed

name: Corollary \refcor.tr

label: thm.drift_general
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.drift_general}
Let $\delta, {\mathcal D} \ge 0$, and $N \in {\mathbb N}$.
Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space. 
Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group, and let $\nu$ be an admissible probability measure on $\Gamma$ with finite first moment.
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite symmetric generating set of $\Gamma$ with $1 \in \Sigma$.



Then, there exists a constant  $\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)>0$ such that for
every faithful, non-elementary and ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical isometric action $\rho:\Gamma \to \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$  satisfying $L(\rho(\Sigma)^N)\ge K_0\delta+1$,
we have
\[
\ell(\nu, \rho)\ge \kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)L(\rho(\Sigma)).
\]
Here $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta}.
head: environment
name: Main theorem I

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U:=\rho(\Sigma)$, and $\mu:=\rho_\ast \nu$.
We may assume that  $1 \in \operatorname{{\rm supp}} \nu$ since otherwise Lemma \ref{lemma.lazy}
reduces the general case to this one at the cost of a factor of $2$.  
To apply Theorem \ref{thm.meta}, we first verify its assumptions and identify the relevant constants. 
We claim that there exist $q=q(\Gamma, \Sigma, \nu) \in {\mathbb N}$ and $\theta_0=\theta_0(\Gamma, \Sigma, \nu) \in (0, 1]$ such that for every faithful isometric action $\rho$ of $\Gamma$ on $X$,
we have
$\min_{u \in \rho(\Sigma)}(\rho_\ast \nu)^{\ast q} \ge \theta_0$.

Indeed, since $1 \in \operatorname{{\rm supp}} \nu$ and $\nu$ is admissible, the support of $\nu^{\ast n}$ is weakly increasing in $n$, and the union of these supports coincides with $\Gamma$.
Moreover, since $\Sigma$ is a finite set,
there exists $q \in {\mathbb N}$ such that $\Sigma \subset \operatorname{{\rm supp}} \nu^{\ast q}$.
Letting $\theta_0:=\min\{\nu^{\ast q}(s) \ : \ s \in \Sigma\}>0$,
we have $\min_{s\in \Sigma}\nu^{\ast q}(s)\ge \theta_0$.
Furthermore, by the injectivity of $\rho$,
we have $\min_{u\in \rho(\Sigma)}(\rho_\ast \nu)^{\ast q}(u)\ge \theta_0$, as required.
By definition, $q$ and $\theta_0$ depend only on $\Gamma$, $\Sigma$, and $\nu$, but not on $\rho$.
Moreover, we have $\rho(\Sigma)^{-1}=\rho(\Sigma)$ since $\Sigma$ is symmetric.




Note that $\mu=\rho_\ast \nu$ has a finite first moment on $(X, d)$ for every $\rho$.
Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm.meta},
letting $\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu):=\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)$,
we obtain
\[
\ell(\nu, \rho)=\ell(\rho_\ast \nu)\ge \kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu) L(\rho(\Sigma)).
\]
This shows the theorem.
\qed
head: manual

label: cor.drift_Hn
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.drift_Hn}
Fix an integer $n \ge 2$ and a real $a \in [1, +\infty)$.
Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group, $\Sigma$ a finite symmetric generating set of $\Gamma$ with $1 \in \Sigma$, 
and 
$\nu$ an admissible, probability measure on $\Gamma$ with a finite first moment. 



Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(n, a, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)>0$ such that the following holds.

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$. 
For every faithful, isometric action $\rho:\Gamma \to \operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ such that $\rho(\Gamma)$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent,
we have
\[
\ell(\nu, \rho)\ge \kappa(n, a, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)L(\rho(\Sigma)).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lemma.independent},
there exists $N=N(n, a)$ such that $L(\rho(\Sigma)^N)\ge K_0\delta +1$,
where $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta}.
Also, the faithful action $\rho$ of $\Gamma$ on $X$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical with ${\mathcal D}={\mathcal D}(n, a)$ by Corollary \ref{cor.Hn}, and   non-elementary by Lemma \ref{lemma.nonelem}.
Note that the hyperbolicity constant $\delta$ is at most that of ${\Bbb H}^2$ (see Section \ref{sec.hadamard}).
Thus, Theorem \ref{thm.drift_general} yields the claim with $\kappa(n, a, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu):=\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, \Gamma, \Sigma, \nu)$.
\qed
head: manual
name: Corollary \refcor.drift_Hn

label: thm.drift2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.drift2}
For every $\delta, {\mathcal D} \ge 0$, $N, m \in {\mathbb N}$,
there exists a constant $\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, m)>0$ such that the following holds:

Let $(X, d)$ be a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic space.
For every finite symmetric set $U$ in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}} (X)$ with $\#U=m$ such that $\<U\>$ is non-elementary, ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical, 
and $L(U^N)\ge  K_0\delta+1$,
we have
\[
\ell(\mu_U)\ge \kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, m)L(U).
\]
Here $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta}.

In fact, we have
\[
\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, m)=\frac{1}{16M (2m)^{2M}},
\]
where $M$ is a positive integer depending only on $\delta$, ${\mathcal D}$, and $N$.
head: environment
name: Main theorem II

title: Proof
body_md:
To apply Theorem \ref{thm.meta} we verify its assumption and identify the relevant constants. 
We may assume that  $1 \in \operatorname{{\rm supp}} \mu_U$ since otherwise we use Lemma \ref{lemma.lazy}
at the cost of replacing $m$ by $2m$ in below. 
By definition, we have $\min_{u \in U}\mu_U(u)=1/m$ and thus $q=1$ and $\theta_0=1/m$.
Applying Theorem \ref{thm.meta},
we obtain the claim with the constant $\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, m):=\kappa_\star(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, q, \theta_0)$.
Furthermore, we have
\[
\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N, m)=\frac{\theta_0^{2M}}{16qM}=\frac{1}{16M m^{2M}},
\]
where $M=M(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N)$.
This shows the claim.
\qed

label: cor.srwHn
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.srwHn}
Let $n \in {\mathbb N}$, $a\in [1, +\infty)$, and $m \in {\mathbb N}$.
Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(n, a, m)>0$ such that the following holds:

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$.
For every finite symmetric set $U$ in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ with $\# U=m$, such that $\<U\>$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent, 
we have
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(n, a, m)L(U).
\]

Moreover, we have
\[
\kappa(n, a, m) = \frac{1}{16M (2m)^{2M}},
\]
where $M$ is a positive integer depending only on $n$ and $a$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lemma.independent}, there exists $N=N(n, a)\in {\mathbb N}$ such that $L(U^N)\ge K_0\delta+1$ where $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta} and $\delta$ denotes the hyperbolicity constant of ${\Bbb H}^2$.
Furthermore, 
the action of $\<U\>$ on $X$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical where ${\mathcal D}={\mathcal D}(n, a)$ by Corollary \ref{cor.Hn}, and
non-elementary by Lemma \ref{lemma.nonelem}.
Therefore, Theorem \ref{thm.drift2} implies the claim.
\qed

label: question.constant
title: Question
head: environment

label: cor.dichotomy
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.dichotomy}
Let $n \in {\mathbb N}$, $a\in [1, +\infty)$, and $m \in {\mathbb N}$.
Then, there exists a constant $c(n, a, m)>0$ such that the following holds:

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional Hadamard manifold with sectional curvature $K_X \in [-a^2, -1]$.
For every finite set $U$ in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}(X)$ with $\# U=m$ and $U=U^{-1}$ such that $\<U\>$ is discrete,
exactly one of the following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $\ell(\mu_U)=0$ if $\<U\>$ is virtually nilpotent. 
\item $\ell(\mu_U) \ge c(n, a, m)$ if $\<U\>$ is non-virtually-nilpotent.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set 
$$c(n, a, m):={\varepsilon}(n, a) \kappa(n, a, m),$$ where ${\varepsilon}(n, a)$ is a Margulis constant of $X$ and $\kappa(n, a, m)$ is the constant in Corollary \ref{cor.srwHn}. 

If $\<U\>$ is discrete and non-virtually-nilpotent,
then by the Margulis lemma, we have $L(U) \ge {\varepsilon}(n, a)$ \cite[Section 8.3]{BGS}.
Thus, Corollary \ref{cor.srwHn} implies that 
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge {\varepsilon}(n, a) \kappa(n, a, m)=c(n, a, m).
\]

On the other hand, if $\<U\>$ is virtually nilpotent, 
then the Poisson boundary of $(\<U\>, \mu_U)$ is trivial (cf.\ \cite[Proposition 1.4]{KV}).
Note that $\mu_U$ is symmetric since $U=U^{-1}$.
Considering the word norm $|\cdot\,|_U$ on $\<U\>$ with respect to $U$,
the corresponding drift $\ell_U(\mu_U)$ is equal to $0$ by \cite[Corollary 2]{KL}.
Since $d(o, g o) \le (\max_{u \in U}d(o, uo))|g|_U$ for all $g \in \<U\>$,
we have $\ell(\mu_U)=0$.
\qed
head: manual

label: remark.dichotomy
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark.dichotomy}
The conclusion  of Corollary \ref{cor.dichotomy} may fail if we do not assume $U= U^{-1}$.
Indeed, take $U$ to consist of  a single element generating an infinite cyclic group.

Also, we can not remove the assumption that $\<U\>$ is discrete.
Indeed, in  ${\Bbb H}^n$, there exists a finitely generated non-virtually-nilpotent solvable group $\<U\>$ in a parabolic subgroup in $\operatorname{{\rm Isom}}({\Bbb H}^n)$ such that
$\< U\>$ is not discrete and  $\ell(\mu_U)=0$.

label: cor.drift.hyp.gp
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.drift.hyp.gp}
Fix  $\delta \ge 0$ and positive integers  $m_0$, and $m$.
There exists a constant $\kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)>0$ such that the 
following holds. 

Let $G$ be a hyperbolic group, and $U_0$ a finite symmetric generating
set of $G$ such that $\# U_0=m_0$ and that ${\rm Cay}(G,U_0)$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic.
For every finite symmetric set $U$ in $G$ with $\# U=m$ such that $\<U\>$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$, 
we consider the $\mu_U$-random walk on ${\rm Cay}(G, U_0)$.


Then, we have
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m) L(U).
\]
head: environment
name: Linear estimate in Hyperbolic group

title: Proof
body_md:
To show the claim, we assume that $1\in U$ and use Lemma \ref{lemma.lazy} if necessary.
We first show that there exists a positive integer $N$, which depends only 
on $\delta, m_0$ such that for every finite symmetric set $U$ with non-elementary $\<U\>$, 
we have
$L(U^N) \ge K_0 \delta +1$.
Indeed, since $1\in U$, the sequence 
$$U \subset U^2 \subset U^3 \subset \cdots$$
 is increasing. It is strictly increasing 
 since otherwise it would stabilize and $\langle U\rangle$ would be finite, 
which is impossible.
Hence $U^n$ contains at least $n$ points
for every integer $n>0$. 

Now define an integer $N:=\lceil{m_0^{K_0 \delta +1}\rceil}+1$. 
Let $x\in {\rm Cay}(G, U_0)$ be an arbitrary point.  
Since the set $U^N$ contains at least $N$ points, 
the set $U^Nx$  is not contained in the ball 
of radius $K_0 \delta +1 $ centered at $x$ 
in ${\rm Cay}(G,U_0)$ since the ball
contains at most $m_0^{K_0 \delta +1}$ points. 
This implies that  $L(U^N) \ge K_0 \delta +1$. 

As we noted before the statement, the action of $G$ on ${\rm Cay}(G,U_0)$ is ${\mathcal D}$-weakly acylindrical
for ${\mathcal D}={\mathcal D}(\delta, m_0)$. 
We apply Theorem \ref{thm.drift2} to this action. 
Set $\kappa_1(\delta, m_0,m)=\kappa(\delta, {\mathcal D}, N,m)$, and 
we obtain the desired inequality. Here we used that both $\mathcal D, N$ depend
only on $\delta, m_0$. 
\qed
head: manual

label: cor.hyperbolic.spec
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.hyperbolic.spec}
Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group, and $U_0$ a finite symmetric generating set of $G$. 
For each integer $m\ge 4$,
we define
$$
\mathcal{L}(G,U_0,m):=\Big\{\ell(\mu _U) \ : \ U\subset G, \ \# U \le m, \ U=U^{-1}, \ \text{$\<U\>$ is non-elementary} \Big\}.
$$
Then,
the set $\mathcal{L}(G,U_0,m)$
is discrete and unbounded. 


In fact,
for each $A>0$ and each $m \ge 2$,
there are only finitely many symmetric $U$ up to conjugation by an element in $G$ with $\# U\le m$ such that $\<U\>$ is non-elementary and that $\ell(\mu_U) \le A$.


In particular, 
for each $A>0$, the set $\mathcal{L}(G,U_0,m) \cap (0,A]$ is finite.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta$ denote the hyperbolicity constant of ${\rm Cay}(G, U_0)$, and $m_0:=\# U_0$.
We show that for each $A>0$ and for each $m \ge 2$,
there are only finitely many $U$ up to conjugation by an element in $G$ with $\# U=m$ such that $\<U\>$ is non-elementary and that $\ell(\mu_U) \le A$.
Since $\ell(\mu_U)$ is invariant under conjugating $U$ in $G$,
the set $\mathcal{L}(G, U_0, m) \cap (0, A]$ is finite.

Applying to Corollary \ref{cor.drift.hyp.gp},
we have a constant
$\kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)>0$ 
such that
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)L(U).
\]
Therefore, 
if $\ell (\mu_U) \le A$, then 
$L(U) \le A/\kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)$.
Then, there exists an element $g$ in $G$ such that $g^{-1}Ug$ is contained in the ball of radius
$A/\kappa_1(\delta, m_0, m)+1$ centered at $1$ in ${\rm Cay}(G, U_0)$.
Thus, 
there are only finitely many such $U$ up to conjugation by an element in $G$.
In particular, this implies that for each  $A>0$,
the set $\mathcal{L}(G, U_0, m) \cap (0, A]$ is finite, so that the set $\mathcal{L}(G, U_0, m)$ is discrete.

Finally, the set is unbounded since $L(U)$ is unbounded if we vary $U$.
To see this, take two independent infinite order 
elements $g,h \in G$, set 
\[
U=\{g^n, g^{-n}, h^n, h^{-n}\}
\]
and let $n \to \infty$, so that the set $\mathcal{L}(G, U_0, m)$ is infinite and unbounded. 
\qed
head: manual

label: rem.KKS
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem.KKS}
Corollary \ref{cor.hyperbolic.spec} may be viewed as a partial generalization
of \cite[Theorem D]{KKS} on free groups to 
hyperbolic groups, possibly with torsion.
In \cite{KKS}, they discuss the set of values of {\it generic stretching factors} on finite rank non-abelian free groups (see their definition).

To explain the relation, fix a Cayley graph of a free group of rank $m$ associated to a free basis.
For the simple random walk associated with another free basis, the drift is equal to the generic stretching factor multiplied by $(m-1)/m$ (see \cite[Proof of Theorem 2.2, p.16]{KKS}).

Thus, in our terminology, \cite[Theorem D]{KKS} implies that the drifts obtained by varying the free basis belong to $\frac{1}{N}\mathbb Z$ for some positive integer $N$. We do not know  whether 
the set defined in 
Corollary \ref{cor.hyperbolic.spec} is contained in $r {\mathbb Z}$ for some $r \in {\mathbb R}$ for general hyperbolic groups.
head: environment

label: lemma.mcg
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma.mcg}
There exists a constant $N=N(\mathcal S)$ such that for 
every finite set $U$ in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ with
$\<U\>$ containing a pseudo-Anosov element, 
we have
\[
L(U^N) \ge K_0\delta+1.
\]
Here $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta}, and $\delta$ is the hyperbolicity constant of $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It is known that there exists a constant $N_1=N_1(\mathcal S)$ such that 
if $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element, then
$U^{N_1}$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element $g$ \cite[Theorem 1.1]{M}.

Also, there is a constant $\tau=\tau(\mathcal S)>0$ such that ${\rm tr}(u) \ge \tau$ for every pseudo-Anosov
element $u$ in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ \cite[Proposition 4.6]{MM}.
Hence, for every $n \in {\mathbb N}_0$,
we have $L(U^{N_1 n}) \ge {\rm tr}(g^n) \ge n\tau$ by Lemma \ref{lemma.disp} \eqref{item.trL}.
Letting $n:=\lceil (K_0\delta+1)/\tau \rceil$ and $N:=N_1 n$,
we have
\[
L(U^N) \ge K_0\delta+1.
\]
We note that $N$ depends only on $\mathcal S$.
\qed
head: manual

label: thm.mcg
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.mcg}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least two, and $m \in {\mathbb N}$. 
Let us consider the action of ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ on the curve graph $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$ endowed with the combinatorial path metric.
Then, there exists a constant $\kappa(\mathcal S,m)>0$
such that the following holds:

Let $U$ be a finite symmetric set in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ with $\#U=m$ such that $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element 
and not virtually cyclic. 
Consider the uniform distribution $\mu_U$ on $U$.
Then, we have
$$\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(\mathcal S,m) L(U).$$
head: environment
name: Mapping class groups

title: Proof
body_md:
The curve graph $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic, and the action of ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ on $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$ is $\mathcal D$-weakly acylindrical, where $\delta$ and ${\mathcal D}$ depend only on $\mathcal S$. 
By assumption, $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element.
By Lemma \ref{lemma.mcg}, 
there exists $N=N(\mathcal S) \in {\mathbb N}$, which depends only on $\mathcal S$, such that $L(U^{N}) \ge K_0 \delta +1$.

The elementary closure of every pseudo-Anosov element is virtually ${\mathbb Z}$.
Since by assumption $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element and is not virtually cyclic, 
there exists $u \in \<U\>$ such that $u \notin E(g)$.
Note that $g$ and $ugu^{-1}$ have disjoint sets of fixed points in the boundary of $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$. Indeed, if otherwise, then the diameter of $\pi_{{\rm Ax}(g)}(u{\rm Ax}(g))$ is infinite, which contradicts the (weak) acylindricity of the ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$-action on $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$.
Thus, the action of $\<U\>$ on $\mathcal C (\mathcal S)$ is non-elementary.

Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm.drift2}, we have
$$\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(\delta, \mathcal D, N(\mathcal S), m) L(U).$$
Taking $\kappa(\mathcal S,m)=\kappa(\delta, \mathcal D, N(\mathcal S), m)$ gives the desired conclusion. 
\qed
head: manual

label: cor.gap.mcg
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.gap.mcg}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least two, and 
$m \in {\mathbb N}$. 
Then, there exists a constant $c(\mathcal S, m)>0$ such that the following holds:

For every finite set $U$ in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$ with $\# U=m$ and $U=U^{-1}$,
we have
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
$\ell(\mu_U) \ge c(\mathcal S, m)$, if
$\<U\>$ contains at least one pseudo-Anosov element, and $\< U\>$ is not virtually cyclic.


\item
Otherwise, $\ell(\mu_U)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Gap for $\ell(\mu_U)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal S)$

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) 
Since $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element, 
by Lemma \ref{lemma.mcg}, 
there exists $N=N(\mathcal S)$, which depends only on $\mathcal S$, such that $L(U^{N}) \ge K_0 \delta +1$, where $K_0$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm.meta} and $\delta$ is the hyperbolicity constant of the curve graph $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$.
Hence, by Theorem \ref{thm.mcg}, we have
\[
\ell(\mu_U) \ge \kappa(\mathcal S,m) L(U) \ge \kappa(\mathcal S, m)\frac{K_0 \delta+1}{N(\mathcal S)}.
\]
Letting $c(\mathcal S, m):=\kappa(\mathcal S, m)(K_0\delta+1)/N(\mathcal S)$ yields the desired inequality.


(2) We use the classification of subgroups of mapping class groups.
First, suppose that $\<U\>$ is finite, then its orbit is finite, hence clearly
$\ell(\mu_U)=0$. Second, suppose that 
$\< U\>$ is a reducible subgroup in ${\rm Mod}(\mathcal S)$. Then there is a finite set
of vertices $V$ in $\mathcal C(\mathcal S)$ that is invariant by $\< U\>$.
Again, the orbit by $\< U\>$ is finite, so that $\ell(\mu_U)=0$.
Finally, suppose $\<U\>$ contains a pseudo-Anosov element $g$, and $\<U\>$ is virtually cyclic.
Then, we have $\ell(\mu_U)=0$ (cf.\ the proof of Corollary \ref{cor.dichotomy}).
This completes the argument.
